translations.text: Once Laisrén went with a working party [?] from the community of Clonmacnoise to clean Cluain Caín, a church in the territory of Connacht.
He kept three three-day fasts while cleaning the church.
At the end of the third fast, sleep overcame him in the oratory, and in his sleep he heard the voice saying to him:
'Rise up!' He did not stir the first time. Then he heard the voice again.
At that he raised his head and made the sign of the cross over his face.
He saw that the church he was in was full of light, though part of the night still remained.
And he saw the radiant figure between the chancel screen and the altar.
The figure said to him: 'Come to me!' At that voice the cleric's whole body trembled from the crown of his head to the soles of his feet.
He saw his soul suddenly on the top of his head, and he did not know by what way it had gone out of the body.
He saw that the church was open upward toward heaven, and he saw two angels take him between them and lift him into the air.
Then he saw a host of angels before him. And they saw another host, of demons, with fiery hair [?]
about them, and fire coming out of every limb they had. Three forms appeared to him among the demons.
Some of them had a jet-black form, with fiery barbed spears [?] in their hands, and others had a pitch-black form, with fiery arrows in their hands.
The third group had a shaggy form, with fiery hair through them like the hair of a [?], and fiery darts in their hands.
These three hosts then made a single battle-charge to contest the soul with the angels.
And one of them accused the soul in a single accusation, the length of one breath, without any change of speech, of all the misdeeds he had committed since he was born.
That single accusation seemed to the soul as long as if it lasted for ever [?],
yet the demon spoke nothing but the truth, and did not charge the soul with anything it had confessed to its soul-friend before leaving the body.
An angel of the great host answered the demon on behalf of the soul and said: 'Have you now set out your whole accusation?'
The demon answered, and this is what he said: 'I have not, I have not set out the greater part of it.' The angel answered:
'You cannot make that accusation, since he made his confession and did his penance as his soul-friend directed before leaving the body.
So go away,' said the angel, 'you have no share in this man.' 'If the word of God is true,' said the demon,
'we will not leave like this, for this man did not become a little child, as God commanded him, saying:
"Unless you are converted and become like little children, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven."'
'The word of God is indeed true,' said the angel,
'for this man has not come to the demons to stay; he will carry a warning ahead of us to his companions.'
'Get away from us, then,' said the angel. They went away from him at once.
Then an angel of the great host said to the two angels who were with him: 'Take this man now, so that he may see hell.'
He is then taken northward through a great valley. He travels through it [?] until they saw a distance as great as from the rising of the sun to its setting.
And they saw a great cavern, like the mouth of a cave between two mountains, so that they came to it from above [?].
They go into the cave for a long while, until they came to a great, high, black mountain in front of them at the entrance of hell, and a great valley in the upper part of that mountain.
This is what that valley is like: wide at the bottom, narrow at the top.
That, then, is the door of hell, and the cave is its porch.
And he saw the people of this island, those of them who are in their bodies in rebellion against God [?]. They were in the middle of the valley, weeping.
'Alas, O God!' said the soul. 'Is it a plague that has come after we left?
For all these hosts have died after we left, since the time we set out.' 'Not so,' said the angel,
'but everyone who is in rebellion against God among the living after you, this is what their souls await, and it is quite certain, unless they repent.'
'A question: shall I tell this,' said the man, 'about every soul I see here?' 'No,' said the angel,
'so that they may not despair because of it. But tell them to repent, for everyone who repents and perseveres in it to the end
will not be in this place, but will be in a place protected from this evil, and his repentance will carry him past it.
And moreover, whoever lives in righteousness, it is life he awaits while he is in the body, and it is life in which he will be, if he is steadfast in righteousness.
Tell them, then,' said the angel,
'let him who is in righteousness be steadfast in it, for their thoughts will not last long before death comes. And let him who is in rebellion against God
repent, for God accepts repentance if it is done purely from the heart, and God's mercy will help him.'
After that the man's soul went into hell itself, that is, a sea of fire with an indescribable storm and with indescribable waves on it.
And he saw the souls in that sea, all their heads on fire above it, weeping and lamenting without rest forever.
Some of the souls had fiery nails driven through their tongues, coming out the back of their heads; some of them through their ears; some of them through their eyes.
He also saw some of them with their mouths open, and the demons dragging them with fiery forks in the same way as the three other groups.
The man wanted to know the reason for the punishments. The angel answered him at once, for the angel would answer minds and thoughts:
'The people you see with the fiery nails through their tongues, that is,
people, then, who were not frequent in praising God or in blessing and adoring him, but who were more frequent, however, in falsehood and in weeping [?] and in br[?]
and perjury and blasphemy and words of pride and [?]
